messages:
sam: Quick design review request — updated mock for the API credentials surface. Trying a compact create flow (inline) instead of a modal + a more prominent soft-revoke banner in the empty state. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.local/creds-compact-v2.png maria: Love the compact create idea. Fewer clicks for power users. My worry: discoverability for org admins — will they understand scopes when it's inline? :thinking_face: lee: Technical constraints: inline creation is fine, but we can't fetch org-scopes synchronously for every keystroke. We should lazy-load scopes when the user opens the scope picker to keep initial render fast. Also we need to maintain keyboard focus order when the drawer expands. ada: Accessibility nits: if create is inline, ensure the scope picker is a true combobox with aria-expanded and aria-activedescendant. Also the soft-revoke banner must use aria-live="polite" so screen readers catch the undo affordance. Proposed toast copy: "Key revoked. Undo" (aria-label: "API key revoked. Undo available"). maria: Copy tweak suggestion for the empty state banner: current "No active keys" is too neutral. How about: "No active API keys — create one to start sending requests" with a CTA "Create key" and a secondary "Learn about scopes" link. That could reduce accidental broad-perm keys. sam: Agree. Also thinking of changing the revoke confirmation modal to a softer inline action: when you click Revoke, we collapse the row into a yellow banner with two buttons: "Undo" and "Delete permanently". This keeps users from losing context (and avoids an extra modal). Thoughts? lee: That pattern is okay, but we need to ensure idempotency: accidental multiple revokes shouldn't trigger multiple backend jobs. Recommend optimistic UI + background job, and show state "Revoking..." on the row. If backend fails, we revert with an error banner in the row. ada: For screen readers, collapsing the row into a banner needs an explicit announce. Use role="status" and aria-live="assertive" for the revoke result (but polite for the initial banner). Example snippet we use elsewhere: ```html
API key revoked.
``` sam: Nice. Two microcopy variants to vote on for the inline revoke banner: A) "Key revoked — undo"; B) "Revoked — remove permanently". I slightly prefer A (less scary). maria: +1 A. Also propose adding a small helper text under the create CTA: "Keys are scoped to roles — admins can rotate or limit access later." Might reduce support tickets. lee: One more UX constraint: on Dedicated/Private deployments we need to show region and SLA hints near the key meta (because customers asked why a key behaves differently across envs). Could be an inline pill: "Dedicated — low-latency". ada: Accessibility check: the pill must be keyboard reachable and have a visible focus ring. Also color contrast needs to pass 4.5:1 if it's used inline with text. sam: Action items: (1) I'll push updated mock with inline scope picker and soft-revoke row (new screenshot v2). (2) @lee please confirm lazy-load approach and add the revoke state behavior to the API contract. (3) @ada please write the a11y acceptance criteria for the combobox, revoke banner, and pills. (4) @maria will finalize microcopy. deploy-bot: sam requested review of design branch `feat/creds-compact` — CI passed, staging preview available at https://staging.redwood.local/creds-compact-2187654321 maria: Thanks — I'll draft the final copy and post a short UX spec in the doc tomorrow. If we can land the aria snippets and revoke contract this sprint, we can A/B test compact vs modal on a small cohort. :rocket: sam: Perfect — will follow up with the updated PNG and a short Loom showing keyboard nav. Thanks everyone!
